guardrails.title: Work only in your addon repository
guardrails.rule: Work only in this repository. Kassis core is a dependency, never a file to edit.

guardrails.title: Import only from the SDK and your own code
guardrails.rule: Import only from @kassis/* packages and your own src/. Never resolve host services by name.

guardrails.title: Choose the lowest rung
guardrails.rule: Choose the lowest rung: configuration first, a declarative addon second, code last. State the rung you chose and why in the change summary.

guardrails.title: Declare permissions and audit every write
guardrails.rule: Every route declares a permission in your addon namespace. Every write goes through ctx.data or a host facade and records an audit action declared in the manifest.

guardrails.title: Give every event a schema and handle missing capabilities
guardrails.rule: Every published event has a schema. Every consumed capability handles null, because the addon that provides it can be switched off.

guardrails.title: Make every migration reversible
guardrails.rule: Every migration has a down script, or is marked irreversible with a reason.

guardrails.title: Declare any widened access
guardrails.rule: Never widen permissions, egress hosts or data access without saying so in the change summary.

guardrails.title: Pass certify before you finish
guardrails.rule: Run kassis addon certify before you say you are done, and fix every error. Certify runs check, conformance, build and test, and those results are the only machine evidence.

guardrails.title: Trace every Must requirement
guardrails.rule: Every Must row in REQUIREMENTS.md must be named by at least one test under test/ or one GAPS.md entry. Run kassis-addon requirements before you finish. Certify records machine check adk.requirements-traced and fails with KADK-718 or KADK-719 when tracing fails.

guardrails.title: Document what you built
guardrails.rule: When a change is described by Kassisdoc, update the business page, the technical page, or both, and link the business page from the technical guide. Also update README.md and CHANGELOG.md.

guardrails.title: Do not refactor code you were not asked to change

skills.title: Add a route
skills.description: Add an HTTP route to a Kassis addon with kassis-addon scaffold route. Use when the BRD needs a new GET endpoint, a permission in the addon namespace, and mount wiring from initialize.
skills.body:
# Add a route

## When to use

A Must requirement needs a new HTTP surface on this addon. Prefer a host facade or UI contribution when they already cover the need. Use a route when the addon must expose its own API under `/api/v1/addons/<id>/…`.

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=route --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm `manifest.json` gained `<addon-id>.<name>` under `permissions`.
3. Edit `src/server/routes/<name>.ts` — keep the Express GET stub working, then add the real handler. Every write goes through `ctx.data` or a host facade and records a declared audit action.
4. Confirm `src/server/index.ts` calls `mount<Name>(ctx)` from `initialize`.
5. Add or extend a test under `test/` that names the requirement id (`FR-*` / `NFR-*`).
6. Run `kassis-addon check`, then `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Import host services by name or reach outside `@kassis/*` and this addon's `src/`.
- Skip the permission declaration or mount a route outside the addon namespace.
- Hand-write a parallel router when scaffold already wired the mount.

skills.title: Add a table with a migration
skills.description: Add an owned table and reversible migration with kassis-addon scaffold migration. Use when the addon must store its own rows and declare data.schema, ownedTables, and retention.
skills.body:
# Add a table with a migration

## When to use

A Must requirement needs persistent data that core tables cannot hold. Prefer a core record type or extension point first. Own a table only when the process data is this addon's.

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=migration --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm the manifest sets `data.schema`, a qualified `database.ownedTables` entry, and `data.retention` (`retain` / `archive` / `purge`).
3. Fill `migrations/<nnnn>_<name>.up.sql` and the matching `.down.sql`. Mark irreversible only with an `irreversible:` reason comment when a down script is impossible.
4. Keep queries bounded (pagination / `take`). Do not create private copies of core approval, audit, notification, or user tables.
5. Name the requirement id in a test under `test/` or record the gap in `GAPS.md`.
6. Run `kassis-addon conformance` (checks up/down pairing), `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Leave `ownedTables` empty while creating tables.
- Ship an up script without a down script and without an irreversible reason.
- Expect tier 2 install-time migration runs before host work S2.02; scaffold warns when that applies.

skills.title: Add an event with a schema
skills.description: Publish a domain event with a JSON schema using kassis-addon scaffold event. Use when other addons or core must react to a change this addon owns.
skills.body:
# Add an event with a schema

## When to use

A Must requirement needs a named domain event other code can subscribe to. Every published event must have a schema; undeclared names are refused by the host and the testkit.

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=event --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm `events.publishes` lists `<addon-id>.<name>` with `schemas/<name>.schema.json`.
3. Tighten the schema required fields if the stub (`subjectId`, `summary`) is not enough.
4. Use the generated `publish<Name>` helper from `src/server/events/<name>.ts` — do not call undeclared event names.
5. Add a test that publishes through the testkit and names the requirement id.
6. Run `kassis-addon check`, `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Publish an event name missing from the manifest.
- Omit a schema file or leave `additionalProperties` as a way to skip validation.
- Swallow a missing optional capability without handling null when you consume events or capabilities.

skills.title: Add a job
skills.description: Register a background job handler with kassis-addon scaffold job. Use when work must run asynchronously under a declared job type.
skills.body:
# Add a job

## When to use

A Must requirement needs work that must not run on the request path (retries, batching, deferred side effects). Declare the job type in the manifest and keep the handler idempotent.

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=job --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm `jobs.types` lists `<addon-id>.<name>`.
3. Implement `src/server/jobs/<name>.ts` and keep `register<Name>(ctx)` wired from `initialize`.
4. Make the handler safe to run twice. Give every outbound call a timeout from Settings or the existing caller pattern — do not hardcode AI model or provider choices.
5. Cover the requirement id in `test/` (or `GAPS.md`).
6. Run `kassis-addon check`, `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Enqueue a job type missing from the manifest.
- Rely on module-level mutable state (hot toggle must dispose cleanly).
- Skip audit when the job writes data.

skills.title: Add a UI page
skills.description: Add an addon UI page and nav entry with kassis-addon scaffold ui-page. Use for rung 2 or 3 addons that need a host-sdk page, en/fr locales, and a render test.
skills.body:
# Add a UI page

## When to use

A Must requirement needs an operator-facing screen inside Kassis. Prefer composing `@kassis/host-sdk` components. Use rung 2 (UI) or rung 3 (UI + migrations).

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=ui-page --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm `ui.contributions.nav` gained an entry and `src/ui/index.ts` routes to the page.
3. Edit `src/ui/pages/<name>.tsx` using `@kassis/host-sdk` only — no `@/features/*` or other addon internals.
4. Put every chrome string through the generated locale keys in `src/ui/locales/en.json` and `fr.json`.
5. Keep `test/ui/<name>Page.render.test.ts` green; name the requirement id in a test or `GAPS.md`.
6. Run `kassis-addon check`, `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Hardcode English button or empty-state chrome.
- Import React components from the host app path aliases.
- Scaffold ui-page on a rung 1 (server-only) addon without raising the rung first.

skills.title: Add an MCP tool
skills.description: Declare an MCP tool contribution with kassis-addon scaffold mcp-tool. Use when agents must call this addon through the host MCP surface.
skills.body:
# Add an MCP tool

## When to use

A Must requirement needs a tool agents can call through MCP. The contribution is gated by enablement and signatures; keep the handler thin and permission-aware.

## Steps

1. From the addon root: `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=mcp-tool --name=<kebab-case>`.
2. Confirm `contributions.mcp` points at `dist/mcp/contribution.js` and `src/mcp/tools/<name>.ts` uses `@kassis/mcp-contract`.
3. Implement the handler; refuse when the caller lacks the declared permission.
4. Keep `test/mcp/<name>.mcp.test.ts` green and name the requirement id.
5. Ensure the build emits `dist/mcp/contribution.js` before deploy (default `kassis-addon build` may only bundle `src/server/index.ts` — extend the build when needed).
6. Run `kassis-addon check`, `kassis-addon requirements`, then `kassis-addon certify`.

## Do not

- Register a tool outside the addon id namespace.
- Skip the offline MCP test scaffold writes.
- Assume a disabled addon still exposes the tool — the host fails closed on toggle.
